dedupe_keys.name: africa fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation fapar absolute values dekadal and monthly geotiffs acmad 2012 onwards

description: This dataset gives the absolute fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (fAPAR) over Africa, a measure from 0 for bare soil to 1 for dense healthy vegetation of how much sunlight the canopy absorbs for photosynthesis. The African Centre of Meteorological Applications for Development (ACMAD) shares it on the Humanitarian Data Exchange, derived from optical satellite sensors such as those on Sentinel and PROBA-V as processed by the Copernicus Global Land Service. Maps are provided as monthly and dekadal (ten-day) GeoTIFF files zipped by calendar year, from 2012 to 2024 in the metadata, with the dataset updated about every two weeks. Files of up to about 50 MB per year are free to download without registration under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is continental. Caveats: values saturate over dense tropical forest, arid areas with sparse vegetation are dominated by the soil signal, and the archives preserve the original scanned files, which may need conversion. Simulation uses: vegetation state for crop growth, pasture and drought impact inputs in food supply and early warning models across Africa. Related records: the EDO Combined Drought Indicator (data-edo-combined-drought-indicator) uses fAPAR anomalies with rainfall and soil moisture.
name: Africa fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (fAPAR) absolute values, dekadal and monthly GeoTIFFs (ACMAD, 2012 onwards)
provider: African Centre of Meteorological Applications for Development (ACMAD), from Copernicus Global Land Service products (HDX)
schema_summary: GeoTIFF rasters of absolute fAPAR (0 to 1) per dekad and month
